evidence: Draft B better serves the local LLM community by naming specific models (Gemma variants, Qwen-2.5-vl-7b) and concrete failure modes (missing list items, 10^9 vs 109 confusion) that readers can recognize and test against. It explicitly acknowledges missing context (hardware, document quality, model versions, May 2025 date) rather than abstracting away these details, which preserves credibility and invites informed discussion. Draft B frames the question as a genuine gap-finding exercise ('are there any compact models known to handle...what tradeoffs have you encountered') rather than a generic invitation. Draft A generalizes to 'a set of Google's models and another 7B parameter vision-language model,' losing the specificity needed for community members to map their own experiences onto the problem. Both preserve facts accurately, but B's concrete naming and explicit uncertainty acknowledgment make it more actionable for a technical audience seeking to contribute real-world comparisons.
